solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Toe-curling jewellery item found in church: value unknown

indicators.note: the jewellery item is found inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England
a ring is a piece of jewellery
worth means value
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: An embarrassing piece of jewellery turns up in a church collection, and nobody knows what it is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toe-curling makes you squirm with embarrassment, which is exactly what cringeworthy describes.

clue.text: Grape originally acclaimed by jazz fan with degree

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

indicators.note: originally points to the very beginning of the word acclaimed, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of acclaimed
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A grape variety first praised by a jazz-loving graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts the A beside CAT, so CAT comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Catawba is a North American grape variety, red-skinned and used for wine and juice.

clue.text: Expecting win, they may fail badly

indicators.note: doing something badly suggests a messed-up version, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hoping for a win while the opposing side may well flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' reads as anticipating a victory, but it is the pregnancy sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the family way is an old-fashioned idiom for being pregnant, which is also what expecting means.

clue.text: European king wearing anorak

indicators.note: the anorak is worn around the king, so the king's letter sits inside

parts.note: anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, a geek
R is short for Latin rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch from Europe dressed in a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an anorak is both a hooded jacket and a nerdy obsessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek is a native of Greece, a country in Europe, so one kind of European.

clue.text: Argumentative type runs into manipulator

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation goes into the word for a manipulator

parts.note: a wangler gets things by devious manipulation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome person bumps into someone who pulls strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangler is someone who disputes noisily or at length, a quarrelsome arguer.

clue.text: Not quite the way to put to flight!

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a route is a way to go

explanation.surface: An exclamation that this is not exactly the proper way to chase an enemy off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an army is to defeat it so thoroughly that it flees in disorder.

clue.text: Bulk of ambassador's son protecting a provider of 1 down

indicators.note: the ambassador's and son's letters wrap around the rest like a guard

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador; with 's it gives HES
a vine provides grapes, and 1 down is a grape
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: The size of a diplomat's son as he guards a fruiting plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 down answer is a grape, so its provider is a vine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulk and heaviness both mean great weight or mass.

clue.text: Complaint jointly suffered by scrubbers, perhaps?

definitions.text: Complaint jointly suffered by scrubbers, perhaps?

parts.words: Complaint jointly suffered by scrubbers, perhaps?
parts.note: a joint ailment of the knee, named after domestic servants who knelt to scrub floors

explanation.walkthrough: 'jointly' looks like 'shared together' but means affecting a joint; 'scrubbers' are floor-cleaning maids.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemaid's knee is prepatellar bursitis, inflammation from long kneeling, once common among servants scrubbing floors.

clue.text: Stated reason French writer briefly creates heraldic beast

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for a reason is heard as a single letter

parts.note: why asks for a reason

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Jules Verne was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A spoken reason why a French author, in a few words, invents a beast for coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a two-legged winged dragon used as a charge in heraldry.

clue.text: Student's notes on boy king

indicators.note: in a down-or-across sense the notes are placed after, on the end of, the king

parts.note: Tutankhamun, often called Tut, became pharaoh as a boy
E and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A pupil's jottings about the young pharaoh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student's' reads as possessive but is 'Student is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a person being taught by a tutor, which is a kind of learner.

clue.text: Flattering article penned by a mostly uninspiring politician

indicators.note: the article is written inside, enclosed by the remaining letters
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: dull means uninspiring
a Tory is a British Conservative politician
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sycophantic piece of writing by a rather boring politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is just the word a.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory means expressing excessive praise, so it is fawning and flattering.

clue.text: Remains of cake grew mouldy

indicators.note: mouldy food has gone off and decayed, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Leftover cake has gone mouldy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is what remains after something is destroyed, the broken debris.

clue.text: It's a girl's sort of paper

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's kind of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin soft paper, used for wrapping or as a disposable handkerchief.

clue.text: A bill plugging public vehicles: you can count on them

indicators.note: the bill is pushed in like a plug filling a hole

parts.note: buses are public transport vehicles
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A demand for payment stuffed into the town's buses, which are reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you can count on them' reads as reliability, but it means counting with them literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for arithmetic, so people literally count on abacuses.

clue.text: Say more than anyone else — to the greatest degree

parts.note: to utter is to say
most means more than anyone else

explanation.surface: Speaking more than everyone else, as far as one possibly can.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, uttermost means the furthest or highest possible extent, as in trying one's uttermost.

clue.text: Sailors reportedly spot bishops, say, on board

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: to see is to spot, and bishops are an example of chessmen, pieces on a board, giving see men

explanation.surface: Mariners apparently catch sight of clergy coming aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship for sailors, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are sailors, people who work on ships.

clue.text: Bovine creature reportedly off, ultimately to Zimbabwean city

indicators.note: reportedly means heard rather than seen, so the sound is used

parts.note: a bull is a bovine creature; said aloud, bull away gives the city's opening sounds
away means off, gone

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter

parts.note: last letter of to

explanation.surface: A cow-like animal is said to be heading for an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulawayo is the second largest city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Person of high birth stealing Italian poet's heart

indicators.note: stealing takes something away, so a letter is removed
the heart of the word is its middle letter, the one taken

parts.note: Ludovico Ariosto was the Italian poet of Orlando Furioso

explanation.surface: A nobleman pinches the heart of an Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristo is informal for an aristocrat, someone of noble birth.

clue.text: Even though I put in wager, a learner comes first

indicators.note: the article and learner are placed at the front of the rest

parts.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: the I is put inside the word for a wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Someone admits placing a bet even though a beginner got there first.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning although or even though.

clue.text: Traitor in Paris who attracts support

parts.note: qui is French for who
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: A traitor in the French capital who draws backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A quisling is a collaborator who betrays his country, after the Norwegian Vidkun Quisling.

clue.text: Eminent man's cry of surprise about foreign currency

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cry goes round the currency

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A distinguished man exclaims at an exchange rate abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank, originally a Spanish nobleman.

clue.text: Medieval horse, black, with three feet?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: A dark horse from the Middle Ages, oddly given three feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three feet' looks like a lame horse's legs but is a measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayard was the magic bay steed of medieval French romance, ridden by Renaud and his brothers.

clue.text: Disney film buff cheers one in South Africa

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan
ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An enthusiast toasts someone in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Walt Disney animated feature set to classical music.

clue.text: Bloomer made by union leader initially entering dump

indicators.note: the initials go into the word for a dump

parts.note: a tip is a British rubbish dump

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each word it covers

parts.note: first letter of union
first letter of leader

explanation.surface: A blunder by a trade union boss going into a rubbish heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a mistake but here means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip is a spring flower, something that blooms, hence a bloomer.

clue.text: Festivity a habitual convict upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: an old lag is a British slang term for a habitual criminal

explanation.surface: A party disturbs a career criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special social occasion.

clue.text: Lover shortly meeting a sailor from the East

parts.note: in a mo means in a moment, shortly

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the East means read right to left

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A lover soon to meet a sailor coming from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Like wizened old men in the fourth row

parts.note: a line is a row
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Wrinkled old fellows sitting in the fourth row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizened elderly faces are wrinkled, which is to say lined.

clue.text: He rates sport wrongly — it's way above us!

indicators.note: doing it wrongly suggests the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A man misjudges sport, and the topic is far beyond us.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere is the layer of the atmosphere from about ten to fifty kilometres high, far overhead.
